title: VLM Run Gateway: Run GLM-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR-2, dots.mocr with an OpenAI Compatible API
gist: VLM Run launched a Gateway that puts open-weight OCR/VLM models (DeepSeek-OCR-2, GLM-OCR, dots.mocr, PaddleOCR-VL) behind a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint plus MCP server, arguing document-parsing costs can drop ~10x versus defaulting to frontier VLMs, with orchestration (rasterization, batching, retries) built in to remove the switching-cost friction that keeps teams locked into one model.

insights.claim: Most teams still default to frontier VLMs for OCR and document parsing not because they perform best, but because researching, evaluating, and deploying open-weight alternatives is too much operational hassle.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: Signals a real wedge for OCR-routing infrastructure products: the bottleneck is evaluation/deployment tooling, not model capability, which is a solvable and monetizable gap.
insights.locator: Open-weight OCR VLMs have advanced significantly

insights.claim: Once a team builds preprocessing, batching, parsing, retries, and evaluation around one VLM's API, switching to a better model that ships later becomes expensive for reasons unrelated to the new model's capability.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: The moat in applied-AI infra is integration/orchestration lock-in, not the underlying model weights -- vendors who abstract that layer can commoditize the model choice underneath them.

insights.claim: No single OCR/VLM model wins across use cases: healthcare forms, construction drawings, and legal contracts each impose different accuracy requirements driven by domain, scan quality, language, and layout density.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: Supports a multi-model routing/gateway architecture over any single best-in-class OCR model bet; investors evaluating document-AI vendors should check whether they route across models or are single-model dependent.

insights.claim: Switching from frontier VLMs to open-weight OCR models (DeepSeek OCR 2, GLM-OCR, dots.mocr, Paddle OCR VL, PP-OCRv6) via a one-line API change can process 100K+ pages for under $60.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: Concrete unit economics investors can use to model document-processing cost lines for AI-heavy back-office/document-automation businesses.

insights.claim: At production scale, using open-weight OCR VLMs instead of frontier VLMs for extraction, OCR, layout, and parsing tasks cuts cost by roughly 10x.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: A 10x cost gap on a narrow, high-volume task category is large enough to reshape vendor selection for any company running document pipelines at scale.
insights.quote: the cost difference is significant, often 10x

insights.claim: Frontier VLMs remain the better choice for open-ended reasoning tasks ('figure out what this means') but are an expensive, often unnecessary default for narrow extraction, OCR, layout, and parsing tasks ('parse this').
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: Pushes back on the reflexive use of general-purpose frontier models for commoditized subtasks -- a segmentation an investor can apply when assessing which AI workloads are price-competed versus reasoning-differentiated.

insights.claim: VLM Run Gateway puts multiple open-weight OCR/VLM models behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint and handles document orchestration end-to-end: rasterizing PDFs, distributing pages across workers, preserving page order, streaming completed pages, retrying failures, and isolating out-of-memory errors.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: A drop-in OpenAI-compatible interface lowers switching costs to near zero, directly attacking the lock-in dynamic the same article identifies as the reason teams stay on frontier VLMs.

insights.claim: VLM Run ships an MCP server (gateway.vlm.run/mcp) with a read_document tool so any MCP-compatible agent client -- including Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode -- can consume visual/document content natively and cost-effectively.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: Positions cheap OCR as infrastructure for agentic coding/automation tools, an adjacent distribution channel beyond direct API customers watch for MCP becoming a standard integration surface for document AI.

insights.claim: Every Gateway response includes a usage.cost field, letting users run the same documents through multiple models and compare exact costs directly rather than relying on vendor claims.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: Built-in cost transparency reduces the evaluation friction the piece cites as the core reason teams avoid switching models, reinforcing the product's core value proposition.

insights.claim: The Gateway's OCR catalog spans very small specialized models -- PP-OCRv6 (22M), GLM-OCR and PaddleOCR-VL (0.9B), dots.mocr and DeepSeek-OCR-2 (3B), Florence-2-base-ft (0.2B) -- none larger than 3B parameters, far smaller than typical frontier general-purpose VLMs.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: Sub-3B specialized OCR models achieving usable accuracy is evidence that narrow-task model efficiency is outpacing the need for ever-larger general models, relevant to compute-demand forecasts for narrow AI tasks.

insights.claim: The Gateway is expanding beyond OCR to host other open-weight visual and audio models, including Qwen3.5-0.8B, Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B, and Parakeet ASR, positioning it as a broader open-weight model routing layer rather than an OCR-only tool.
insights.speaker: Chukwuma Nwaugha
insights.so_what: Watch whether VLM Run generalizes into a multi-modal open-weight inference gateway competing with broader model-serving platforms, not just an OCR cost play.
